transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samantha Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Mark Reynolds (Helix VP Infra), Sonia Gupta (Helix Legal), Liam O'Connor (Helix Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Helix Procurement)

Summary:
Quick procurement/Legal run-through of MSA and DPA items, SLA targets, pricing approval timeline, and onboarding checklist. Customer is leaning toward a Dedicated/reserved capacity conversation but wants clarity on data residency, KMS, SOC2, and escalation SLA. Next steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA + SOW, SOC2 artifacts, security questionnaire answers, and schedule CISO call.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we appreciate ya. I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Samantha on the technical side and Priya from customer success.
[00:12] Mark: Hi Jordan, thanks. We'll do quick intros - I'm Mark, VP Infrastructure at Helix.
[00:18] Sonia: Sonia here, legal counsel, I'll be driving the MSA redlines.
[00:22] Liam: Liam, head of ML, will be driving the pilot and perf benchmarks.
[00:27] Aisha: Aisha, procurement, I'll own vendor onboarding and pricing approvals.
[00:31] Jordan: Great, goal for today is to go through the MSA/DPA high level, SLA ask, any security blockers, and agree on next steps for procurement.
[01:05] Samantha: I'll chime in on technical stuff as we hit it - especially around data-at-rest encryption, KMS, and network isolation for private deployments.
[01:40] Sonia: I sent over Helix's standard MSA comments earlier, just to align expectations. A few must-haves: audit logs, data deletion commitments, and indemnity language.
[02:10] Jordan: Totally, and Redwood has a standard MSA and DPA. We'll circulate a redlined version but quick note: for private deployments we typically support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or HSM, and we can commit to retention and deletion terms in the DPA.
[02:43] Mark: On the infra side, we're most concerned about data residency and the ability to run in our VPC or on-prem. Will that require a separate private contract?
[03:05] Samantha: For private we do a private control-plane option — you can host in your VPC or on-prem. There's a slightly different onboarding and ops SLA, usually covered under our Private offering and enterprise license. I know earlier we called it Redwood Private, sometimes folk say 'Redwood Dedicate' in notes — that's the same family.
[03:42] Liam: For the pilot, we want to do a 2-week perf benchmark with our prompt set and 99th percentile latency targets. If we don't meet the target, what's the remediation?
[04:05] Jordan: We typically define pilot acceptance criteria in the SOW — if it misses, we do joint tuning: model variant, quantization profile, and batching adjustments. We can also include a credit back clause if SLA isn't met during production after rollout.
[04:40] Aisha: Speaking of SLAs — what uptime/latency SLAs does Redwood offer and how do they differ between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[05:03] Samantha: Hosted API has a standard 99.5% uptime for API endpoints, Dedicated reserved capacity comes with higher targets — typically 99.9% depending on contract, and Private deployments are negotiated given customer infra. For latency, we define target medians and p99S in the SOW and have escalation paths for sustained regressions.
[05:30] Sonia: We need contractual language for escalation and remedies — like service credits tied to p99 violations and a mutual termination right after repeated failures.
[05:55] Jordan: Yep, we have standard service credit language and can scope it to the Dedicated contract. For Private, we work with your legal team on tailored SLO clauses.
[06:25] Mark: On security, can you confirm SOC 2 Type II and whether you have penetration test reports and an incident response plan?
[06:40] Samantha: We have SOC 2 Type II — I'll share the most recent report. We also have pen test summaries and an incident response runbook; for customers we can provide redacted artifacts and an NDA if needed.
[07:05] Sonia: We'll need the full SOC2, plus answers to our security questionnaire. Also encryption at rest and in transit — how is KMS handled?
[07:25] Samantha: For Hosted we manage keys by default but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or bring-your-own HSM in Private deployments. There are some limitations for certain accelerators but we document them in the onboarding playbook.
[07:49] Liam: Any chance of token-level filtering or prefix caching affecting privacy? We want to ensure no cross-tenant leakage in KV cache or prefix cache.
[08:10] Samantha: The runtime uses per-tenant KV caches and we have strict isolation controls; we can include that in the DPA notes. Sometimes the transcript label says 'k-v cache' or 'kv cache' in docs — so apologies for any typos in earlier notes.
[08:35] Aisha: Procurement governance question — what's your pricing model for a pilot vs committed Dedicated capacity? We need a clear path to escalate if pilot is successful.
[08:52] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits and discounts. We'll include a pricing sheet that lays out pilot pricing, conversion to committed rates, and a step-down path. We'll also include a tiered volume discount schedule.
[09:18] Sonia: About liability cap and indemnities — Helix prefers a higher cap for regulated data processors; is Redwood open to raising the cap for certain data classes?
[09:35] Jordan: We can negotiate caps tied to contract value; for regulated workloads we usually land on a higher cap with an enterprise license. We'll flag that for the legal team.
[09:55] Mark: On onboarding timeline, procurement needs the vendor questionnaire answered and MSA redlines within two weeks to hit our June procurement window.
[10:12] Jordan: Understood. We'll aim to get the redlined MSA and SOC2 by next week.
[10:30] Samantha: Technical items to include in the security pack: network diagrams for Private deployment, KMS integration steps, evidence of encryption, and pen test summary.
[11:05] Liam: For the pilot we also want a benchmark runbook and a sample prompt set evaluation template, so results are comparable.
[11:27] Samantha: We'll share a benchmark template; note that quantization and kernel selection can change perf characteristics, we'll enumerate recommended model variants.
[12:00] Sonia: How about data deletion on request — can you demonstrate irreversible deletion from logs and KV caches?
[12:18] Samantha: Yes, deletion APIs exist and we can demonstrate processes — though for backups and logs there's usually a retention window which we can specify in the contract.
[12:40] Aisha: Any third-party subprocessors? We need a list for the DPA.
[12:50] Jordan: We'll provide the subprocessors list — infra providers, telemetry vendors, etc.
[13:15] Mark: One sticking point — our security team wants an on-prem option for inference to ensure no data leaves our network. How realistic is an air-gapped deployment?
[13:35] Samantha: We support on-prem package for Enterprise customers, it's more involved — separate contract, installation window, and ongoing support fees. It is feasible, but we'd need a project plan and resource commitments.
[14:05] Sonia: If we go on-prem, we need guarantees on code escrow and support SLAs.
[14:20] Jordan: We can discuss code escrow and tailored SLAs; that typically shows up in Private Enterprise SOWs.
[15:00] Liam: Quick question about telemetry — can we disable telemetry or limit PII in logs?
[15:15] Samantha: Telemetry can be adjusted; for Private deployments we can reduce or disable telemetry and ensure logs are forwarded to your log cluster.
[15:40] Aisha: Back to pricing approvals — procurement needs the expected monthly spend for pilot and forecasted 3-month and 12-month run rates. Can you provide that breakdown?
[16:00] Jordan: We'll include a pricing workbook with pilot estimates and committed scenarios plus a cost/per-token breakdown and example workload math.
[16:20] Sonia: Also need to confirm export controls and data residency language — Helix operates in EU and US and has some APAC clients.
[16:35] Samantha: We can include regional deployment options and data residency clauses. For Hosted we run in multiple regions; for Dedicated you can pin region.
[17:05] Mark: One more legal ops note — our legal team prefers to negotiate MSA and DPA concurrently rather than separate back-and-forths. Is that ok?
[17:20] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll send both with redlines so you can review together.
[17:40] Liam: Regarding benchmarks — what tooling do you use to measure p99 and p50? We need reproducible metrics.
[17:55] Samantha: We use internal load harnesses; we'll provide a harness script and instructions so you can reproduce the runs.
[18:22] Sonia: If Redwood is using subprocessors in EU, we need SCCs or equivalent — please include.
[18:40] Jordan: We'll include SCCs if needed and work with your legal team on transfer mechanisms.
[19:05] Aisha: Procurement checklist — vendor questionnaire, security docs, MSA redline, pricing approval, vendor onboarding packet. Who owns the onboarding packet?
[19:20] Priya: Redwood will provide the onboarding packet and playbook; we'll align on dates and required contacts.
[19:40] Mark: Let's talk escalation — we need an SLA contact list and on-call schedule for incidents affecting production.
[20:00] Samantha: We'll provide an escalation matrix and on-call rota for Dedicated and Private customers; for Hosted we have an NOC 24/7 and Enterprise customers get a named escalation contact.
[20:35] Sonia: Regarding data processing, we need a clause for audit rights. Helix may request an annual audit.
[20:50] Jordan: We typically accommodate audit rights subject to scope and NDA; we'll include standard audit language in the MSA.
[21:20] Liam: Any constraints on model variants for private deployment? Some GPUs don't support certain quantization kernels.
[21:40] Samantha: Right — kernel selection and quant support depend on hardware; we'll list supported quant levels per accelerator in the onboarding doc, and we can do a compatibility matrix.
[22:05] Aisha: For pilot approval, procurement needs two reference customers and their contact info. Can you provide references?
[22:20] Jordan: Yes, we'll share two references in a redacted form; one is in fintech, another in healthcare.
[22:45] Sonia: On indemnity, we might request IP carve-outs — this will show up in our markups.
[23:00] Jordan: Noted, we'll look for those markups.
[23:25] Mark: Timeline recap — we need the paperwork in one week to hit procurement window. Pilot planned to start after pricing approval.
[23:45] Jordan: Confirming Redwood will aim to get SOC2 and redlined MSA out by 2025-06-13.
[24:00] Priya: I'll follow up to schedule the CISO deep-dive and make sure we have the right stakeholders.
[24:22] Liam: One technical caveat — when doing benchmarks, please include cold-start times in the runbook, sometimes p99 is driven by cold starts.
[24:45] Samantha: Good call; we'll include cold-start measurements and sample warm-up scripts.
[25:10] Sonia: A question about termination assistance — if Helix terminates, what data handoff and assistance do you offer?
[25:30] Jordan: We provide termination assistance periods defined in the SOW, with data export in agreed formats and a runbook for handover.
[26:00] Aisha: For procurement approval, do we need to sign separate SAs for each region?
[26:18] Jordan: Not usually — region clauses in the MSA/DPA suffice, but for on-prem or specialized regions we might need addenda.
[26:45] Mark: Ok, any remaining blockers from legal or security?
[27:00] Sonia: We'll review the redline and security pack; our blockers are likely to be indemnity cap and audit rights.
[27:20] Jordan: Understood — we'll propose options.
[27:40] Priya: I'll capture open items and owners after the call.
[28:05] Samantha: I'll start assembling the security pack and SOC2 artifacts.
[28:30] Jordan: And I'll produce the redlined MSA and proposed SOW.
[28:50] Aisha: Procurement target decision date is 2025-06-20, we'll confirm internally and let you know.
[29:10] Jordan: Great — to summarize next steps: redline, SOC2, pricing workbook, references, security questionnaire answers, schedule CISO call.
[29:45] Mark: Thanks everyone, we'll loop in our CFO if pricing needs further approval.
[30:00] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up via email and update CRM.

(There are a few moments of cross-talk and brief clarifications as attachments and links are shared - "MSA draft link", "SOC2 redacted link", "pricing workbook link")

[35:00] Samantha: Quick tech note — for the pilot we'll recommend a mixed model: smaller model for latency-sensitive paths and a higher-quality model for complex generations; that reduces cost.
[35:30] Liam: That helps — we'll include both path criteria in the SOW.
[36:05] Sonia: Please mark up the MSA with the higher liability cap option so we can see the delta.
[36:25] Jordan: We'll include two liability cap options in the redline.
[37:00] Aisha: Any special procurement terms for payment? Net30 vs Net45? Helix prefers Net45 for new vendors.
[37:15] Jordan: Standard is Net30, but we can be flexible for enterprise deals — we'll flag to finance.
[38:00] Mark: Last question — onboarding time for Dedicated vs Private?
[38:18] Samantha: Dedicated onboarding usually 4-6 weeks; Private/on-prem tends to be 8-12 weeks depending on site readiness.
[38:45] Priya: We'll need hostnames, IP allowlists, and an IAM contact for onboarding.
[39:05] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else?
[39:20] Sonia: We'll wait for the redlines, security pack, and pricing. If anything changes we'll reach out.
[39:35] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll produce deliverables in the timelines discussed.

End of call.
